summary.text: Saint Barlaam was a monk connected with Saint Alexis of Moscow and the establishment of the Vladychny Monastery at Serpukhov.

blocks.text: The Russian Church’s monastic department says that his birthplace, parents, and place of tonsure are unknown. Its narrative begins in 1360. He served as the cell attendant of Saint Alexis, the metropolitan.
blocks.locator: Opening paragraphs on lost origins and relationship with Alexis

blocks.text: The monastery’s tradition attributes its establishment to a command heard from an icon of the Theotokos. Saint Alexis sent Saint Barlaam to find a site. Saint Barlaam oversaw construction and the emerging monastic community; the account includes visions and miraculous events.
blocks.locator: Foundation narrative and paragraphs on building the monastery

blocks.text: The received life describes blindness and failing health near the end of his life. It dates his peaceful repose to May 5, 1377, and says Saint Alexis buried him at the church porch. It does not describe martyrdom.

blocks.text: His memory is preserved chiefly through the monastery’s founding narrative and veneration. Much of his earlier biography was not recorded. The OCA calendar independently commemorates him on May 5.
